subject.title: fix(acp): exec approvals target the matching concurrent prompt

question: Should ACP treat every present exec approval toolCallId as authoritative, failing closed on missing or duplicate matches while retaining session-only fallback solely for legacy events that omit the identifier?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but this rule determines which concurrent ACP interaction may receive an execution authorization prompt and therefore requires explicit owner acceptance of the security boundary and compatibility fallback.

options.title: Approve authoritative IDs
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed explicit-ID policy and the omitted-ID compatibility fallback, then merge after rebasing and exact-head validation.

options.title: Require stronger identity binding
options.body: Pause the PR and require a run-scoped or protocol-level correlation contract before changing approval routing.

recommendation.title: Approve authoritative IDs
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed explicit-ID policy and the omitted-ID compatibility fallback, then merge after rebasing and exact-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP exec-permission relay and are best positioned to confirm its intended correlation and fallback policy.
